3. Learned counsel for the petitioner(s) submitted that the crux of the matter is that the petitioner(s)
herein, is/are (erstwhile) public servant(s), the cause of action qua the instant dispute pertains to the year 2012-14, and the impugned FIR was filed at a belated stage in the year 2021.

Further,
learned counsel for the petitioner(s) submitted that the complainant filed a complaint before Magistrate, Sarwad and as a result, under the exercise of powers expounded under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. the impugned FIR(s) were made to be registered against the petitioner(s),

wherein,
allegations were leveled that the petitioner is involved in illegal siphoning of government funds,
forgery and fabrication of bills

. 
4. In this backdrop, learned counsel has placed reliance upon the investigation report undersigned by the Collector and the Anti- Corruption Bureau (Annexure-2 & 3), and has submitted that no case is made out against the petitioner(s).

Lastly, learned counsel has submitted that the impugned FIR(s), are registered merely on [2024:RJ-JP:34451] (4 of 5) [CRLMP-4982/2021] account of political vindictiveness, with malice intentions to oust the petitioner(s) from their post.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents has submitted that the contentions made qua the delay in lodging the FIR are not tenable, as the office of Panchayat has already filed an FIR, against the missing documents that are ought to be considered, in the instant matter.

6. Further, learned counsel has submitted that the complainant was compelled to submit a complaint before the Magistrate and only after attaining the order under Section 156(3) the said FIR(s) were lodged.
Moreover, subsequent to the said investigation report dated 08.06.2021 a detailed inquiry report dated 12.06.2021, under the directions of eight member committee was passed.
The said report explicitly stated that the work orders as alleged were not conducted/complied.
Hence, the contentions leveled insofar by the learned counsel for the petitioner are conjectural.
7. Withal, it is further submitted that the reliance placed upon Annexure-2 & 3 is distorted, as the said report pertains to distinguishable facts and subject matter.
It is further submitted that qua the instant matter investigation has been duly conducted howsoever, the prosecution sanction is awaited.

8. At this juncture, learned counsel has placed reliance upon the dictum enunciated in 2022 SCC Online SC 1634 titled as Ramesh Chandra Gupta vs. State of U.P and (2022) INSC 1294.
9.

sentences.text: Considering the foregoing facts and circumstances of the case, and taking note of the ratio encapsulated in Ramesh Chandra Gupta (Supra) wherein, it is held that the High Court [2024:RJ-JP:34451] (5 of 5) [CRLMP-4982/2021] must be cautious while exercising the powers expounded in Section 482 Cr.P.C.
It is an undisputed fact that this Court cannot conduct a mini-trial at this stage.

The relevant portion of the afore-stated ratio is reproduced herein below:

entities.text: Vipin Kumar Son Of Shri Mohan Lal Arora vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jp:34451)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Inherent power given to the High Court under Section 482 CrPC is with the purpose and object of advancement of justice.
In case solemn process of Court is sought to be abused by a person with some oblique motive, the Court has to thwart the attempt at the very threshold.

The Court cannot permit a prosecution to go on if the case falls in one of the categories as illustratively enumerated by this Court in State of Haryana v.
Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335.

entities.text:
State of Haryana v.
Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Judicial process is a solemn proceeding which cannot be allowed to be converted into an instrument of operation or harassment."

10. Moreover, considering the nature of allegations leveled against the petitioner(s) in the FIR,
especially taking note of the fact that the impugned FIR(s) are made to register only after interference of the Magistrate, this Court is not inclined to interfere in the instant matter.
11. Accordingly, the instant petition(s) is/are dismissed.
Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
